payload.friendly_name: Test doctrine: mock boundary and red-first value
payload.purpose_context: Two test-quality failures keep recurring in consumer missions: tests that mock code the system under test owns (a stub once manufactured a state the real code could never reach and triggered a false data-loss alarm), and pro-forma red-first tests that only restate configuration and later fail only when someone changes it on purpose. This mission adds a foundation directive that mocks may only sit at the responsibility border, with an explicit allow-list, and scopes the red-first rule to behaviour with lasting regression risk, letting a real run or an existing gate be the evidence for config and glue work. The sibling testing tactics, the review guidance and the doctrine graph are reconciled so no surface contradicts the new rules.
payload.purpose_tldr: Give reviewers and agents a citable rule for where tests may mock, and limit red-first tests to work with a lasting regression risk.

payload.question: Which collaborators may a test mock or stub?

payload.final_answer: Operator ruling 2026-11-20: widened allow-list — another domain/bounded context, filesystem, database, network/external APIs, clock, randomness, git/process, and narrow system cases (DTO validation, hook/notification sends). Everything else inside the responsibility border runs for real.

payload.question: When is a red-first test required, and what replaces it otherwise?

payload.final_answer: Operator ruling 2026-11-20: real-run or existing-gate evidence REPLACES the red-first test for config/glue work. Red-first is required only for lasting regression risk (product logic, gate/classifier scripts, invariants, security/permission policy). Add an [evidenced-by-run] delivery label beside [build]/[ratchet]/[folded], and the long-term-value question. Reviewers flag pure config-restatement tests as waste.

payload.question: Which pack tier holds the new guidance?

payload.final_answer: Operator ruling 2026-11-12/2026-11-20: general rule in foundation (and testing for atdd-adversarial-acceptance); Spec Kitty house specifics (CI-workflow worked example) in internal.

payload.question: May DIRECTIVE_041 be edited in this mission?

payload.final_answer: Operator ruling 2026-11-20: yes, within this mission, keeping the change minimal (no separate PR).

payload.question: Which issues does the mission cover?

payload.final_answer: One mission: #216 + #209 with #151 folded in (record the red failure text; choose a red shape that does not break collection; invert bug-encoding characterization tests; the xfail(strict) cross-WP note from #218). #154 stays out.
